items.title: TastyIgniter allows Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Unrestricted file upload in Media Manager
items.description:
### Summary
Media manager accepts `.htaccess` file which can be used to perform RCE.

### Details
The file upload functionality from media manager somehow accepts `.htaccess` file. This file could be used to allow any extension to run PHP command. By doing so, it is possible to perform RCE.

### PoC
- Login as Admin
- Create a `.htaccess` file with the following code.

```
<FilesMatch "\.jpg$">
    SetHandler application/x-httpd-php
</FilesMatch>
```
- Upload the `.htaccess` file via the Media Manager.

Request
```
POST /admin/media_manager HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8888
Content-Length: 357
sec-ch-ua-platform: "Linux"
X-CSRF-TOKEN: 2vv3ZKpvfj2SkbbJzqmf8G053mNXqPLktxqd5eMx

items.description:
### Summary
**Where:** `POST /admin/mail_templates/edit/{id}` → body field  
**Who can trigger:** Any admin user with `Admin.MailTemplates` permission  
**Impact:** Arbitrary PHP execution on the server — full RCE

### Details
The Mail templates is vulnerable to SSTI and did not perform an validation and sanitization.

### PoC

- login as admin
- create new mail template with following command

```
@php echo shell_exec('echo "RCE Executed";id'); @endphp
```  

- save the request
- execute the request using `X-IGNITER-REQUEST-HANDLER: onTestTemplate`

items.title: fulgur allows Unbounded string-set value accumulation causes memory/CPU exhaustion (denial of service)
items.description:
`fulgur` converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that
processes input supplied by many tenants. In versions from 0.4.4 up to (but not
including) the patched release, the CSS `string-set` named-string values
resolved from a document were accumulated per element with no memory budget,
letting a small crafted document amplify into large retained memory (and the CPU
to copy it) — a denial of service.

A `string-set` value is attacker-controlled: it is resolved from an element's
own text (`content(text)`), from one of its attributes (`attr(...)`), or from a
CSS string literal. fulgur accumulated these values per element in two unbounded
places:

1. **Store (default path).** For every element that matches a `string-set` rule,
   fulgur pushes a copy of the resolved value into a store that is retained for
   the whole render and cloned again downstream into a per-node lookup

items.title: livewire-powergrid: SQL injection via sortDirection in naturalSort queries
items.description:
## [Description]

The public Livewire property `sortDirection` is interpolated **verbatim** into a
raw SQL `ORDER BY` clause and is not restricted to `asc`/`desc`, allowing arbitrary
SQL injection through `POST /livewire/update`.

**Data flow**

- **Source** — `src/Concerns/Sorting.php`: `public string $sortDirection;` is a
  Livewire-bound property with no whitelist/validation (it is only assigned and
  flipped by `reverseSort()`), so it is fully attacker-controlled via the standard
  Livewire update endpoint.

  ```

items.title: laradocs  Command injection via unescaped Node.js binary path in KaTeX SSR
items.description:
### Summary
Local command injection (CWE-78) in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a `proc_open()` command string.

### Affected versions
>= 0.4.0, < 1.0.0

### Patched versions
>= 1.0.0 (fixed in commit `100cb1e`)

### Impact
When rendering KaTeX math **server-side**, Laradocs invoked Node via `proc_open()` with a command string in which the Node binary argument was not passed through `escapeshellarg()`.

`MarkdownPipelineFactory` constructs `KatexExtension` with the configured binary, which the render path resolved as:

```php
$node = $this->nodeBin ?? 'node';
$cmd = $node . ' ' . escapeshellarg($tmpFile) . ' ' . escapeshellarg($input);
```

`$this->nodeBin` comes from `Config::nullableString('laradocs.parser.katex.node_bin')`. Both possible sources — the configured `node_bin` value, or the `'node'` default resolved from `PATH` — are operator-controlled

items.title: @waline/client vulnerable to stored XSS through unsanitized comment edit previews
items.description:
### Summary

`@waline/client` renders the comment editor's live preview with `marked` and no sanitizer (`utils/markdown.ts`), and the preview is injected with `v-html`.

When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (`orig`).

Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTML in their own session: an unauthenticated commenter achieves privilege-escalation stored XSS against a moderator with a single Edit click.

`packages/client/src/utils/markdown.ts:18-37` renders markdown with `marked` and returns the raw HTML with no sanitization (the client bundles no DOMPurify):

items.title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
items.description:
### Impact

`verify_envelope_bsp()` derived its trust anchor from the message it was
verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted
`wsse:BinarySecurityToken`, validated **only** that certificate's not-before /
not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate.
There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning.

A successful `verify_envelope_bsp()` therefore proved only that the envelope was
signed by *whoever supplied the embedded certificate* — never that it was signed
by a *trusted* party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a
forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification.
Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be
impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass).

items.title: TwigView FileLoader may allow arbitrary file reads through user-controlled template paths
items.description:
### Impact
If `FileLoader::findTemplate()` is supplied un-validated user controlled data, arbitrary files can be read.

### Patches
1.3.3 and 2.1.2 contain a fix for this issue.

### Workarounds
Don't supply user controlled data to `include` and `extends` tags.

items.title: GitHub CLI gh codespace jupyter may allow code execution via unvalidated URLs from malicious Codespaces
items.description:
### Summary

A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow remote code execution when users connect to a malicious Codespace using the `gh codespace jupyter` command. The command opens JupyterLab by launching a URL in the user's browser, but that URL is supplied by a process running inside the Codespace and the CLI opens it without validating it.

The browser launcher accepts `vscode://` and `vscode-insiders://` links, so a malicious Codespace can return a crafted `vscode://` URL. The CLI opens the link, the operating system hands it to VS Code, and VS Code acts on it, which can lead to code execution on the user's workstation.

This is a variant of [CVE-2024-52308](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p2h2-3vg9-4p87). That remediation validated the SSH connection details for `gh codespace ssh` and `gh codespace logs`, but did not cover the equivalent Jupyter

items.title: github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp permits denial of service through a malformed IPv4 payload length
items.description: In github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp/dhcpv4/nclient4, BroadcastRawUDPConn.ReadFrom does not validate that the IPv4 payload length is sufficient to hold a UDP header before calculating the DHCP payload length. A frame with an IPv4 total-length field specifying fewer than eight payload bytes results in a negative DHCP length, causing a panic in buf.Consume due to a negative slice bound.

items.title: etcd: CRL enforcement bypass on gRPC listener when `--listen-client-http-urls` is configured
items.description:
### Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

When etcd is configured with `--listen-client-http-urls` to split the HTTP and gRPC client endpoints onto separate listeners, the `--client-crl-file` Certificate Revocation List is not enforced on the gRPC listener. A client presenting a revoked certificate is correctly rejected by the HTTP endpoint but continues to authenticate successfully over gRPC.

### Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

This vulnerability is patched in the following versions:

- etcd 3.6.13
- etcd 3.5.32

### Workarounds
_Is there a way for users to fix or remediate the vulnerability without upgrading?_

items.title: ruflo MCP bridge allows unauthenticated remote code execution in default Docker Compose deployments
items.description:
The MCP bridge shipping in ruflo/docker-compose.yml exposed POST /mcp with no authentication. The docker-compose defaults bound the bridge and MongoDB to all interfaces. Combined, an unauthenticated network attacker could invoke tools/call → terminal_execute inside the bridge container, obtain a shell as node (uid 1000), read every provider API key from the container env, spawn attacker-controlled swarms on the victim's keys, and persist a poisoned pattern into the AgentDB learning store that steers future AI outputs for all users of the instance.

The tool blocklist that mentions terminal_execute was enforced only in the autopilot flow. POST /mcp and POST /mcp/:group bypassed it.

Fixed in ADR-166 Phase 1-3 (branch security/adr-166-mcp-bridge-rce, PR #2521):
- Bind loopback by default; fail-closed on public-bind opt-in without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN
- Bearer auth middleware (timingSafeEqual con

items.description:
### Summary

The standalone FFmpeg execution endpoint `plugin/API/standAlone/ffmpeg.json.php` builds a shell command string that is passed to `execAsync()` and run via `nohup sh -c "<command>"`. When the decrypted `codeToExec` payload produces a non-empty `avideoPath`, the endpoint appends a completion hook of the form:

```
 && php <script> notify=<escaped-json> notifyCode=<codeToExec->notifyCode> callback=<codeToExec->callback>
```

The `notify` value on this line is wrapped with `escapeshellarg()`, but the two adjacent fields `notifyCode` and `callback` are concatenated raw. Both fields originate from the same decrypted, attacker-controlled `codeToExec` object as `ffmpegCommand`, but neither passes through the `sanitizeFFmpegCommand()` denylist (only `ffmpegCommand` does) and neither is shell-escaped. items.title: Cakephp twig-view unserialize Twig filter allows arbitrary object deserialization
items.description:
### Impact
The `unserialize` filter has no restriction on which classes are allowed. This can be used as a deserialization remote-code-execution gadget.

### Patches
1.3.3 and 2.1.2 contain a fix for this issue. The fix may impact backwards compatibility if you are relying on deserializing PHP objects in your templates.

### Workarounds
Don't use the `unserialize` filter.
